key_insight: A cycle-consistent neural surrogate can both predict tokamak edge plasma fields and infer the underlying operating parameters, while also quantifying uncertainty to support reliable use.
engineering_relevance: This enables millisecond-scale edge-plasma predictions for parameter scans, optimization, real-time control, and digital-twin workflows that would be impractical with full SOLPS-ITER runs.
method: Conditional U-Net forward model maps five control inputs to 2D SOLPS-ITER plasma-state fields.
Optimization-based inverse model is built on the frozen forward network and trained with cycle-consistency.
An ensemble MLP predicts midplane and divertor profiles with uncertainty estimates to flag sparse regions.
evidence_signal: The forward model reports normalized RMSE below 2.6% and Pearson correlations above 0.95, while cycle-consistency lifts average cyclical R² from 0.59 to 0.99 and all five control parameters are recovered with Pearson r ≥ 0.97.
watch_item: Performance depends on training data coverage; uncertainty flags can indicate where additional simulations are still needed, and cold-start inversion can fail without a database warm start.
paper_title: Cycle-Consistent and Uncertainty-Aware Neural Surrogates for Tokamak Edge Plasmas
